newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds were flat towards the end of the day as profit-taking emerged ahead of the decision by the US Federal Open Market Committee.

"The likely rise in the US official (discount) rate will have a bad influence over European rates too, even though it could support the dollar against the mark," a dealer said. An announcement from the FOMC is expected about 1815 GMT.
Today's decision by the Bank of Spain to leave its key money rate unchanged did not disappoint financial markets, which now expect an official rate cut on October 3.
But dealers said there was a flattening of the yield curve.

"We saw more profit-taking in the five-year bonds segment," a dealer explained. The 7.40 bond was trading at 100.75/84 at a yield of 7.06 percent. But the December three year-bond contract was up five basis points at 99.32.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds rose to 193 basis points from yesterday's low of 186, but dealers remain positive and see it even lower in the coming days.
For the 10-year future chartists peg support at 105.11 and resistance at 105.55, then at 105.78.
